fields.text: A Method without a Miracle
lines: A Method without a Miracle

fields.text:
The completed Arkbird cooperation record had supplied a scientific method, not a promise that a platform would always be there. Lev kept that distinction on the first page. Anton wanted the learner to understand why the modest packet mattered; Daria wanted her able to repeat a measurement without borrowing confidence from an impressive name. fields.text: An Appointment Kept
lines: An Appointment Kept

fields.text:
Anton had an appointment he wanted to postpone. He called it an awkward hour between two useful tasks, which told Irina that the tasks were easier for him to describe than the appointment. Lev offered to accompany him. Daria asked whether he wanted company or merely somebody else to make the decision. The board had acquired a comfortable place for Anton's help. A review might confirm that arrangement, change it or ask him to explain what he had stopped saying aloud. Irina could protect the appointment in the shared plan, leaving its purpose for Anton to disclose, or move the day's work privately until nobody outside the crew noticed an absence.

The hearing review is not a test of Anton's courage. Irina remembers the thin tone after the headset and asks what he wants the next clinician to know, rather than when he will return to the old work.

fields.text: The Weak Line Answers
lines: The Weak Line Answers

fields.text:
The weak reply arrived while Irina was trying to establish a clear approach. It answered a question Lev had abandoned several minutes earlier. She almost treated the familiar words as a new clearance. Anton, working on the ground beside the receiver, asked which question had actually been answered. Lev started the exchange again and Irina held until she understood it. After landing, Daria drew two separate lines on the board: what the pilot had heard and what the controller had intended. Neither line accused anyone of lying. Anton offered to speak privately with the tired operator while the next task continued. Irina could accept that kindness or reopen the misunderstanding with the whole shift. The aircraft was back. The next crew still needed an answer that belonged to the question they were asking.

The crew once repaired Lev's missed call quietly. Irina cannot tell whether that kindness taught him to ask for help sooner or taught the rest of them how much could disappear from an account.

Lev thought the call had ended when the weak voice answered his last question. Anton reached for the next sheet, and Irina almost followed him. Then Daria raised a hand. The voice had answered a different question, one they had stopped asking several minutes earlier. Nobody had lied. A tired operator and an impatient room had simply reached different parts of the conversation. Lev could reopen the exchange and expose the misunderstanding, or let Anton speak privately with the operator while the room continued. Irina looked at the empty chair beside the receiver. It was easy to demand patience from a person who had nowhere to put down the work already waiting.

fields.text: Yesterday's Date
lines: Yesterday's Date

fields.text:
The component had been checked, but the board gave yesterday's date and the person who remembered doing it had gone off shift. Daria found an intermittent connection that disappeared whenever she held the cable still. Anton fetched a lamp with his back to the receiver, sparing his ears the continuing hiss. Irina could ask him to find the earlier checker privately, or stop the shared handover while Daria established what the entry meant. Lev wanted the person who had written the date to speak before the mistake became a rumor. Neither option made a damaged connection safe by itself; Daria kept it on the bench. The decision was whether the correction would travel with the work or depend on the four remembering whom they had told. Anton rested the lamp where a new apprentice could hold it.

Irina once limited what her signature could mean. The old choice makes it harder to mistake today's useful check for proof that yesterday's account was already sound.

fields.text: The Empty Hook
lines: The Empty Hook

fields.text:
Anton took his gloves off the hook and put them in a drawer. Irina felt an absurd urge to stop him, as if the hook were a promise the room had made. He said he was tired of visitors learning his old job before they asked what he did now. Lev had arranged a place at the teaching table. Daria had left practical work there, not a ceremonial task to keep him occupied. Anton could explain the change himself, allowing strangers to ask clumsy questions, or the crew could protect him with a concise introduction and let him choose when the longer account became public. The empty hook would remain either way.

The quiet reassignment helped after the headset strain. Anton says that being protected then should not mean everybody else gets to decide how his work is described forever.

fields.text: The Envelope beside the Receiver
lines: The Envelope beside the Receiver

fields.text:
Lev left the envelope closed until Irina sat down. It contained an account whose neat cover invited a more confident answer than the notes inside supported. Anton set a second chair beside the receiver so nobody would have to explain the uncertainty standing alone. Daria asked who would sign the question if the answer failed to arrive. They were not deciding a country's policy in the small room. They were deciding how a personal voice would survive being passed onward by people with more authority and less time. Irina could leave the qualification on the shared cover, or call the next recipient privately and trust them to carry it without the paper's help.

The learner once repeated the uncertain measurement instead of treating a method as a miracle. Irina wants the next recipient to inherit the same permission to ask again.

fields.text: Who Will Answer the Next Voice
lines: Who Will Answer the Next Voice

fields.text:
Lev balanced the receiver on a borrowed table while Daria found four chairs. The country's capitulation had changed the work the station could perform, but it had not explained the uncertain exchange waiting in Irina's folder. Anton offered to take the first questions from the incoming operator. Irina knew the kindness and the danger of letting him carry every difficult answer. They could preserve their uncertainty where others would have to see it, or protect the exhausted debrief and pass onward a narrower account. Neither would restore a state or prove a national outcome. Daria poured the tea before it went cold, leaving a small ordinary task inside a room whose larger promises had changed.

fields.text:
Other participants had entered the fighting. Lev crossed out a heading that made two countries sound like the whole conflict and left room for what the room could not know. Irina's own exchange was difficult enough to explain. Anton offered to answer the next operator's questions, and Daria asked whether he meant to help or to make everybody else's embarrassment disappear. They could share the uncertainty openly or keep the debrief protected and give the incoming shift a bounded account. Neither choice authorized them to promise peace, judge a winner or decide what distant allies intended. The new operator needed a useful place to begin, not a confident ending the four could not establish.

The country's mandate had withheld its declaration. Anton repeated the wording carefully: a national decision, not evidence that the other side had agreed to everything. Lev placed the incoming shift's folder beside an exchange whose missing words still needed to remain missing. Irina felt relief and the urge to let it improve the account. Daria asked her to wait until the tea was poured before answering anyone. They could preserve the uncertainty openly or protect the four people's debrief and send only what they could defend. An avoided declaration had not made an uncertain voice certain. The new operator would need a method that remained useful after relief stopped being the strongest feeling in the room.

The reciprocal exchange had closed this declaration route. Lev wrote that much and stopped before adding a promise about every future voice. Irina could understand the wish for a complete ending, particularly while Anton smiled at news that let the room breathe more easily. Daria brought the next shift's folder back to the center of the table. A difficult exchange remained to be described, including words none of them could confirm. Irina could share the uncertainty with the new operator or protect the personal debrief and send a narrower account. They were allowed to be relieved. They were still responsible for deciding which parts of that relief belonged in another person's instructions.

fields.text:
A flash beyond the cloud made Irina begin a turn before Lev completed the warning. The next instruction broke under static. Anton, listening from the ground, asked Lev to repeat the direction rather than supply the part he could not hear. Irina held the changed heading until she understood where she was being sent; the other aircraft became a pale shape beyond her wing and then disappeared into weather again. At the debrief Daria asked which observations would help the next crew survive the same uncertainty. Anton sat beside the receiver, with no suggestion that his useful question had restored his old flying role. The war between the two countries was real. Its existence did not identify every light or voice. Irina could preserve the uncertain exchange openly or protect the exhausted conversation within the four. Lev left room beneath the words he had actually received.

The next operator arrived before the four had agreed how to describe the difficult exchange. Irina had written what she remembered, Lev had marked the words he could not confirm and Daria had made tea nobody touched. Anton offered to take the questions. He was good at making another person's embarrassment feel survivable; he was less good at refusing to carry all of it himself. The newcomer needed an account that would remain useful after the familiar faces left. Irina could ask the four to share their uncertainty openly, or keep a protected debrief and give the next shift only the part they could stand behind together. Both meant leaving something unfinished.

The reciprocal exchange had closed this declaration route. Lev wrote that much and stopped before adding a promise about every future voice. Irina could understand the wish for a complete ending, particularly while Anton smiled at news that let the room breathe more easily. Daria brought the next shift's folder back to the center of the table. A difficult exchange remained to be described, including words none of them could confirm. Irina could share the uncertainty with the new operator or protect the personal debrief and send a narrower account. They were allowed to be relieved. They were still responsible for deciding which parts of that relief belonged in another person's instructions.

fields.text:
A flash beyond the cloud made Irina begin a turn before Lev completed the warning. The next instruction broke under static. Anton, listening from the ground, asked Lev to repeat the direction rather than supply the part he could not hear. Irina held the changed heading until she understood where she was being sent; the other aircraft became a pale shape beyond her wing and then disappeared into weather again. At the debrief Daria asked which observations would help the next crew survive the same uncertainty. Anton sat beside the receiver, with no suggestion that his useful question had restored his old flying role. The war between the two countries was real. Its existence did not identify every light or voice. Irina could preserve the uncertain exchange openly or protect the exhausted conversation within the four. Lev left room beneath the words he had actually received.

The next operator arrived before the four had agreed how to describe the difficult exchange. Irina had written what she remembered, Lev had marked the words he could not confirm and Daria had made tea nobody touched. Anton offered to take the questions. He was good at making another person's embarrassment feel survivable; he was less good at refusing to carry all of it himself. The newcomer needed an account that would remain useful after the familiar faces left. Irina could ask the four to share their uncertainty openly, or keep a protected debrief and give the next shift only the part they could stand behind together. Both meant leaving something unfinished.

fields.text: The Person before the Voice
lines: The Person before the Voice

fields.text:
Anton asked the new operators to introduce themselves before putting on the classroom headsets. One expected a trick and gave a call number. Anton waited until Lev supplied his own name first. The lesson was not about remembering everyone perfectly. It was about noticing that a weak reply came from a person whose hesitation might have a reason beyond incompetence. Irina listened from the back while Daria watched an apprentice adjust a chair without being asked. Anton could use his own experience to make the lesson concrete, or teach the method while keeping the experience private. Irina would need to support either choice without turning gratitude into a demand for disclosure.

Irina remembers the medical restriction after the feedback injury. The knowledge makes her careful, not entitled: Anton can choose which parts of that experience strangers are allowed to hear.

fields.text: The Instructor's Spare Pencil
lines: The Instructor's Spare Pencil

fields.text:
Lev's old radio instructor died after a long illness. The family sent a small packet containing a spare pencil and a note explaining that he had always carried two because a learner would forget one. Lev held it as though it were difficult equipment. Anton remembered a man impatient with elegant answers and unexpectedly patient with frightened people. Daria asked whether the family wanted anything returned. Irina thought the next class might welcome the story, then noticed Lev had not yet spoken about it even to them. A death outside the crew had left a place inside it. They could ask permission to share the memory, or allow the pencil to remain a private thing rather than make every loss teach somebody a lesson.

They once protected an appointment without owning its purpose. Irina offers Lev the same ordinary space now, without asking when he will be ready to explain.

fields.text: Room for Another Name
lines: Room for Another Name

fields.text:
The new apprentice could not find a place for her name. The board still carried the four familiar ones beside tasks now taught by other people. Irina had stopped noticing how much authority the old handwriting claimed. Daria offered a clean cloth, and Anton objected that erasing a line did not have to mean forgetting who had done the work. Lev drew a fresh column. They could leave a visible history with the new names, showing where responsibility had changed hands, or keep the familiar board and arrange the apprentice's place privately until she felt ready. Irina looked at her first small line in the corner. Someone had once made room without knowing what she would become.

The spare pencil sits beside the cloth. Lev says that keeping a memory should leave someone else room to begin, not make a person who has gone impossible to replace.

fields.text: The Board They Leave
lines: The Board They Leave

fields.text:
The board was ready before the room was. A new learner had written a question beside a component and left enough space for the answer to change. Daria approved the spacing, which made Anton laugh until she asked him to improve it. Lev put the spare receiver where someone could reach it from the extra chair. Irina had imagined a final explanation that would make all their choices fit together. Instead the learner wanted to know who she should ask when the written method stopped helping. They could leave the names of people willing to answer and a history of questions that had remained open, or a clear signed account that kept the difficult personal history within the four.

The new line already contains a question Irina would have phrased differently. She leaves the pencil beside it instead of correcting the learner's voice into her own.

fields.text: The Account They Can Defend
lines: The Account They Can Defend

fields.text: The board is neat and the signed account is useful. Daria has tested what it says, Lev has made the instructions clear and Anton knows how to help the first nervous learner through them. Irina can defend every printed sentence. The difficult conversations are kept elsewhere, among people who remember why a harmless phrase once made somebody look away. That privacy has protected real friendships. It has also left the next crew dependent on names whose history it cannot see. A learner asks whether an exception belongs on the board. Irina answers carefully and notices how much rests on being in the room to answer. The four do not leave in anger. They leave competent work, a protected account and affection that remains strongest inside its familiar circle. The next people will have to decide for themselves which questions can be asked beyond it.

fields.text: The Clips Left Empty
lines: The Clips Left Empty

fields.text: The clips make small sounds as the four remove their papers. All four are alive to take their work elsewhere, and there is no single betrayal large enough to put in a final account. Anton has work he can teach elsewhere. Daria carries a notebook of checks she will make useful to another set of hands. Lev carefully labels the receiver's awkward switch before handing it over. Irina signs what they can still agree on and leaves space beneath it. They have been kind in ways that did not always let the others speak, and honest in ways that did not always let them remain close. The next learner will inherit real skills and a board whose empty places have more than one explanation. Outside, Anton waits until the other three have their belongings. Their goodbyes are ordinary, which makes them harder. Then the familiar voices take different routes home.

Both can make the register more credible, while giving a different audience the first claim on its attention. The clerk places the blank schedule between them and waits for an instruction that can be entered without writing the same space twice.

fields.text: The Third Copy
lines: The Third Copy

fields.text:
The receiving clerk lays three copies of the same staff reservation across the committee table. Each bears a different departmental seal. The chair asks which copy should become the public record; the clerk answers that choosing a copy will not release a single worker. A civil-service representative proposes a hearing at which the receiving offices can challenge the reservation. The defence representative asks for a protected session first, so junior staff can explain how the duplicate promises were made without answering for their superiors in public. Both want a usable register. They disagree about which protection must come first, and the clerk waits with all three copies still open.

fields.text: A Reservation with an Answer

fields.text:
The clerk returns with the same three copies, now attached to a completed receiving period. The committee can trace the service actually performed and the work displaced by it. One of the original departments has asked that its superseded reservation be removed. The chair leaves it in the file. A later reader needs to understand why the office declined a promise as well as why it accepted another. The standing appropriation preserves the selected priority and its continuing burden. It gives the next government a responsible receiving office, rather than permission to count the same staff three times.

fields.text: The Apprentice at the Back of the Room
lines: The Apprentice at the Back of the Room

fields.text:
An apprentice has attended the whole workshop meeting without speaking. When the superintendent begins to close the docket, she asks whether the training release listed beside her name is still real. A repair deadline has already used the reserved hours. The production representative offers an internal arrangement: a senior worker will cover the lessons after the shift. The training secretary asks that the release itself be restored and the delayed productive work recorded openly. Neither proposal gives the workshop an extra person. The apprentice wants the qualification and knows that the worker offering to teach her is already staying late. The board must decide whose promise it will protect.

fields.text: The Qualification and the Waiting Work
lines: The Qualification and the Waiting Work

fields.text:
The apprentice brings a corrected training return to the review. It records the instruction actually received rather than the hours initially reserved. Beside it lies the maintenance queue, including work deliberately left waiting. The superintendent no longer describes both as an unused reserve. The board's chosen policy has become a practical obligation with a cost that somebody can identify. Its improved settlement will support the next period, but it will not erase the delay or create a second shift of trained workers. The apprentice asks that the receiving clerk keep both documents together so her qualification cannot later be used to conceal the work that paid for it.

fields.text: A Timetable Written in Two Inks
lines: A Timetable Written in Two Inks

fields.text:
The dispatch exercise uses two inks for movements whose receiving windows overlap. A civil coordinator has marked the ordinary repair traffic; the military liaison has marked a support reservation. Both lines end at the same receiving desk. When a trainee tries to solve the exercise by moving one line into an unmarked hour, the dispatcher asks who will staff it. The room falls quiet. The civil coordinator proposes published notice periods, so affected services can challenge an exception before preparing their work around it. The liaison proposes a protected urgent channel with an identified officer answerable for every displaced reservation. The exercise needs a rule that somebody can actually follow.

fields.text: The Movement That Was Deliberately Delayed
lines: The Movement That Was Deliberately Delayed

fields.text:
The review includes the movement that the exercise deliberately delayed. Its receiving office has written a short account of the staff and maintenance time released by that decision. The military liaison asks that the report distinguish a refusal from a lost message. The civil coordinator agrees and asks that an accepted exception remain visible for the same reason. The completed service period gives the timetable a tested procedure; it cannot make every requested window available. Under the standing settlement, later dispatchers inherit the chosen priority and its burden, together with a record explaining why one unfulfilled reservation was the responsible result.

fields.text: Three Seconds on a Training Tape
lines: Three Seconds on a Training Tape

fields.text:
A controller stops a recorded handover exercise at a three-second silence. No aircraft is waiting on this channel; the staff are working through a desk rehearsal. The training officer says that the silence allowed a confirmation to arrive. The civil liaison says the receiving office could not tell a deliberate pause from a broken connection. A junior controller asks whether that uncertainty belongs in the open lesson or in a protected instructor's return. Publishing it would let outside receiving offices test the procedure. Protecting the first debrief could make staff more willing to admit how uncertain they were. The tape remains stopped while the committee decides how the lesson will be received.

fields.text: A Pause with a Receiving Rule
lines: A Pause with a Receiving Rule

fields.text:
The controller plays the silent interval again. This time the completed exercise return identifies which office should acknowledge the pause and what happens when its answer does not arrive. Nobody has removed the uncertain three seconds. The watch policy has gained a tested receiving rule while retaining its political or civilian reservation cost. The instructor cautions that a desk exercise proves no aircraft serviceability or operational success. The committee accepts that limit and keeps the unfinished questions beside the final lesson. A later watch can use the procedure without inheriting a claim that quiet on a training tape meant certainty.

fields.text: The Letter without a Receiving Date
lines: The Letter without a Receiving Date

fields.text:
The external-commitments folder contains a letter thanking the government for assistance. The review staff cannot find a corresponding receiving date. One official wants the letter included as evidence of confidence; another asks whether anybody can now explain what was promised. The committee has no authority to manufacture a foreign answer. It can publish a limited renewal schedule around the domestic staff actually available, or first protect a narrower receiving mandate while those staff inspect the old undertaking. The civil-service officer asks that a refusal remain an acceptable return. The military representative agrees, provided the next government can distinguish a refused promise from an obligation quietly abandoned.

lines: A Useful Answer Can Be a Limit

fields.text:

A later government may accept, renegotiate or refuse another undertaking from this record. It will first have to name the receiving office and the work that its promise would displace.

fields.text: The Notebook outside the Sealed Folder
lines: The Notebook outside the Sealed Folder

fields.text:
A technical archivist brings two objects to the review: a sealed programme folder and an ordinary notebook of methods that the researchers used to check their observations. The security officer asks which belongs to the cooperation record. The archivist answers that the notebook can be useful even when the programme's present status permits no new exchange. A civil researcher wants the transferable methods opened to independent scrutiny. The test representative asks for a protected technical return before uncertain results are treated as established knowledge. Two measurements remain unanswered in the notebook's margin, and neither researcher will mark them complete merely to empty the agenda. The committee must decide how to keep useful knowledge without promising a result that the responsible programme has not delivered.

fields.text: The Inspector’s Unused Stamp
lines: The Inspector’s Unused Stamp

fields.text:
The acceptance inspector has brought an unused stamp to the committee. During a receiving exercise, an invoice and a workshop return carried matching totals but different explanations of what had passed inspection. The procurement officer asks whether the discrepancy could have been corrected inside the office. The inspector says it could, and asks who would then know why the stamp was withheld. An open receiving test would let the affected workshops challenge the record. A protected replacement-priority return would let technical staff reconcile it before a disputed entry was treated as a failed delivery. Both routes can preserve the objection. They reserve different authority and impose different costs on the next receiving period.

fields.text: The Instruction during the Rehearsal

fields.text:

The command liaison proposes a narrower delegated mandate with an explicit expiry and a protected channel for the missing answer. Neither wants obedience to depend on an unanswered telephone. The committee must choose which route will receive exceptional instructions, and who will be responsible when the promised confirmation does not come.

fields.text: The Messenger Returns with the Docket
lines: The Messenger Returns with the Docket

fields.text:

The command representative recognizes the reservation but has a second claim against the same hours. fields.text: The Unsigned Instructor’s Note

fields.text:

fields.text: The Shore Office’s Old Maintenance Book

The original allocation sheet has been returned so often that its folds are beginning to tear. The secretary places it beneath the completed national returns. The civil and command shares still total one hundred; what has changed is the government's ability to identify who reserved each period and who must answer for the work it displaced. The inherited intervention, command-reform and scientific-cooperation records remain their own obligations. These national procedures do not erase them. A district representative asks for a further period of civil inspection. The command liaison asks for a bounded support return with the displaced civilian claims kept beside it. The next government can choose either, and must keep a receiving office available when the unanswered requests arrive again.

fields.text: After Ulysses: the Usean brief
lines: After Ulysses: the Usean brief

fields.text:
The sky has been quiet for five months, and nobody trusts it.

Ulysses passed Earth's Roche limit on 8 July 1999 and broke apart over the world. The fragments fell for weeks. Across Usea the official counts are still being revised: towns that no longer appear on the maps, roads cut by craters, rail yards where the dispatchers work by lamplight. The worst of the impacts are behind us. The cost of them is only beginning to arrive.

The ministries have assembled the first postwar brief on [Root.GetLeader]'s desk. It is thick and contradictory. The agriculture office warns that the harvest across the continental interior will fall short for a second season. The interior office reports families walking toward any border that might take them, carrying what they could load onto carts and the roofs of buses. The treasury asks, politely, how the government means to pay for any of it.

Every capital in Usea is reading a brief like this one tonight. Some will answer it with relief convoys and credit lines, some with closed borders, and some with speeches about who is to blame. The choices made in the next three years will decide whether the continent rebuilds together or turns on itself.

Refugee pressure and fallout recovery are now tracked for our government. They are abstract measures of the strain on the state, not a record of impact sites in our provinces.

fields.text: Erusea and the refugee columns
lines: Erusea and the refugee columns

fields.text:
The border posts along the Erusean frontier were built for customs officers and the occasional smuggler. They were never meant for this.

For months the columns have come: farm families from the cratered interior, townspeople whose water supply failed, whole villages that packed up after the second wave of fragments. The camps at the crossings were meant to hold them for a few days. Some families have now been there since the autumn. The district governors send reports that grow shorter and angrier with every week: no more tents, no more flour, no more doctors willing to make the drive.

In Farbanti the cabinet meets late. The interior ministry has drafted an order to close the frontier and turn the columns back. The foreign ministry warns that the neighbours will remember it. The army reminds everyone that it is the army that would have to enforce it. Outside, the radio stations have already taken sides; one plays the order's text as if it had been signed, another reads the names of children born in the camps.

The official chronology records that Erusea stopped taking in refugees on 21 April 2000. Closing the border is that course. Keeping it open under quotas is a provisional alternative that costs recovery and eases the grievance building in our politics.

fields.text: Refugees turn to Central Usea
lines: Refugees turn to Central Usea

fields.text:
The trains from the north arrive full and leave empty.

Since Erusea closed its frontier, the displaced have turned toward Central Usea and its treaty partners. The first families came on foot; now they come by the hundred on requisitioned buses and fishing boats, with addresses written on scraps of paper and the names of relatives who may or may not still be alive. Reception centres in the border provinces have run out of beds. Local councils have started opening schools and sports halls without waiting for permission.

The cabinet is divided. One faction insists that the Federation's standing in Usea depends on being seen to open its doors, and that the camps can be paid for out of the reconstruction budget. Another argues that every allied capital is under the same strain, and that a treaty organization which cannot share burdens in peace will not share them in war. Both factions agree on one thing: Farbanti has chosen to make this our problem, and it has done so on purpose.

fields.text: Erusea closes its border
lines: Erusea closes its border

fields.text:
FARBANTI — The government of Erusea has closed its frontier to refugees, ending months of uncertainty along the continent's busiest crossings.

Border units began turning back columns at dawn. Reporters at the crossings describe lines of vehicles stretching back several kilometres, families sleeping beside their cars, and relief agencies negotiating for permission to deliver water to people who are no longer allowed to enter. The Erusean interior ministry says the closure is temporary and that the country "has carried more than its share" of the Ulysses fallout.

Neighbouring governments have reacted with alarm. Officials in Central Usea say they are preparing for a sharp increase in arrivals. Commentators across the continent are already asking the question that will shape the next three years: if Usea cannot share the burden of a disaster, what will it share instead?

The official chronology records this closure on 21 April 2000.

fields.text: Central Usea offers mediation
lines: Central Usea offers mediation

fields.text:
The proposal arrives through the ordinary diplomatic channels, which is itself a message.

Central Usea suggests talks: refugee quotas shared across the continent, reconstruction credit for the worst-hit Erusean districts, and a standing commission on the status of Stonehenge, the railgun battery built under the FCU's leadership to shoot down Ulysses fragments. The language is careful and generous. The Erusean foreign ministry reads it twice, looking for the condition hidden inside.

Inside the cabinet, the argument is not really about the terms. Accepting means admitting that Erusea needs help from the countries its newspapers blame for its suffering. Refusing means telling the nation that its grievances are not for sale, and leaving the camps and the craters exactly as they are. The generals have opinions. So do the families in the border towns, who have started writing to the palace.

Accepting lowers tension with the treaty powers. Refusing hardens the national mood.

fields.text: Erusea accepts the talks
lines: Erusea accepts the talks

fields.text:
Erusea has agreed to come to the table.

The delegation is small and its instructions are narrow, but it has arrived, and the first session ran past midnight. Our negotiators report that the Erusean side wants credit before quotas and recognition before either. Nobody expects a settlement this year. Still, a channel that was closed is open, and the newspapers in Farbanti have softened their headlines by a degree.

The grievance in Erusea has eased for now. It has not gone away, and the men who profit from it are still in their offices.

fields.text: Erusea refuses the talks
lines: Erusea refuses the talks

fields.text:
Erusea has refused our offer of talks.

The reply was short and was published in Farbanti before it reached us. It accuses the treaty powers of hoarding reconstruction credit, of building Stonehenge with continental money and then keeping it under their own control, and of lecturing a wounded country about its duties. The broadcast versions were less polite than the written one.

Our analysts read the refusal as a sign that Erusean politics now reward confrontation. That is the most dangerous kind of answer: one written for a domestic audience.

fields.text: A continental accord
lines: A continental accord

fields.text:
It was signed in a conference hall that still had tape across its cracked windows from the fragment season.

After three years of quarrels over refugees, credit and the custody of Stonehenge, Erusea and its neighbours have agreed a continental accord. Erusea renounces the use of force over the Ulysses fallout. The treaty powers commit to a shared refugee system and a reconstruction fund that Farbanti will help to administer. The railgun battery stays where it is, under an international commission with Erusean members.

Nobody in the hall pretended to like everyone else. The newspapers in every capital have found something to complain about. But the armies that were massing along the San Salvacion frontier are going back to their barracks, and the camps at the crossings are, for the first time in years, getting smaller.

In the official chronology, the Usean Continental War begins in 2003. In this campaign it has been averted.

fields.text: Erusea invades San Salvacion
lines: Erusea invades San Salvacion

fields.text:
The first reports came from aircraft over the border: columns moving south, too many and too orderly to be refugees.

By evening the Erusean government had confirmed it. Its armies have crossed into San Salvacion, and their objective is no secret. Stonehenge, the eight-gun railgun battery built to break up Ulysses fragments before they reached the ground, stands in San Salvacion's desert. Whoever holds it holds the sky over half the continent.

The official chronology records that Erusea invaded neutral San Salvacion in the summer of 2003 and seized Stonehenge. In this campaign San Salvacion has been a member of Central Usea's treaty organization since 1991, so its partners are now being called to its defence, and the war is continental from its first day.

Radio stations across Usea have interrupted their programming. In the cities, people queue for petrol and tinned food. Many of them remember the fragments falling four years ago, and most assumed the sky had already done the worst it could do to them.

The exact start date of the war is provisional gameplay; the chronology gives only the season.

fields.text: Stonehenge turns on the sky
lines: Stonehenge turns on the sky

fields.text:
The first allied strike package to fly over the San Salvacion desert did not return intact.

Stonehenge was built to break up rock falling from orbit. Its eight railguns were designed to fire on objects travelling many times faster than any aircraft. Now Erusean crews have turned them on the sky over the battlefield, and the effect has been devastating: formations shattered at altitudes that should have been safe, squadrons forced down to treetop height where the anti-aircraft guns are waiting.

Allied air commanders have begun redrawing every flight plan on the continent around a single circle on the map. Inside it, the air belongs to Erusea.

The official chronology records that Erusea seized Stonehenge and used its railguns against aircraft.

fields.text: The Independent State Allied Forces
lines: The Independent State Allied Forces

fields.text:
The emergency session met in a bunker under the capital that had been built for an entirely different war.

Erusea has ignored the demand to withdraw from Stonehenge and San Salvacion. The railguns are already firing on allied aircraft, and the treaty organization's command structure, designed for peacetime exercises and parade reviews, has buckled in the first weeks. Staff officers from five countries are working out of rented offices, passing paper maps between buildings by courier.

The answer on the table is a new allied command with a single headquarters, a single chain of orders and a mandate broad enough for the war that is actually being fought. Its name has been chosen: the Independent State Allied Forces.

The official chronology records that FCU President Robert Sinclair established the ISAF on 22 August 2003. Our treaty organization will become its command.

fields.text: ISAF is founded
lines: ISAF is founded

fields.text:
The Federation of Central Usea has announced the founding of the Independent State Allied Forces, a unified allied command to drive Erusea out of San Salvacion.

The announcement was brief. It listed the member governments, named the command's mission, and declared that ISAF would accept "any nation willing to stand against aggression on this continent." Reporters noted the absence of any timetable.

In Farbanti the reaction was contempt; Erusean broadcasts called the new command a paper alliance sheltering under guns it could not reach. Along the front, allied pilots have begun painting a new insignia on their aircraft. Many of them have already flown into the range of Stonehenge, and some did not come back.

The official chronology records the ISAF's founding on 22 August 2003.

fields.text: ISAF asks for North Point
lines: ISAF asks for North Point

fields.text:
The invitation was delivered by hand, by an officer who had flown in under radio silence.

ISAF asks North Point to join the allied command. The island's harbours and airfields lie beyond the reach of Stonehenge's guns, and its shipyards could repair what the allies are losing on the continent. In the official chronology, ISAF moves its headquarters to North Point on 16 September 2004; the island becomes the place from which the counteroffensive is planned.

Joining would end a neutrality that North Point's government has guarded for decades. It would put the island on Erusea's target lists and its sailors on allied convoys. Declining keeps the war at a distance, for now, and leaves the allies to look elsewhere. The cabinet knows that whichever answer it gives will be remembered.

Declining is a provisional alternative to the official chronology.

fields.text: North Point joins ISAF
lines: North Point joins ISAF

fields.text:
North Point has joined the Independent State Allied Forces.

The island's government announced the decision in a short broadcast that ended with the national anthem. Within hours, allied transport aircraft were landing on its runways. Harbour authorities have begun clearing berths for warships, and dockworkers are being recalled from leave. The war has reached the island's shores, in the form of guests for now.

fields.text: North Point declines
lines: North Point declines

fields.text:
North Point has declined to join ISAF.

The reply was courteous and firm. The island's government will not join a war on the continent while its own defences are untested and its people unconsulted, but it leaves the door open: if the war turns, it says, the question can be asked again. Our staff officers have already started looking at other harbours. None of them is as good.

fields.text: ISAF falls back to Los Canas
lines: ISAF falls back to Los Canas

fields.text:
The retreat has a name now, and the name is Los Canas.

ISAF's first offensive against Stonehenge has failed. The official chronology records that ISAF was pushed back to Los Canas and that its first attack on the battery failed on 14 September 2003. Allied columns are falling back along every road to the coast, covered by whatever aircraft can still fly. Supply depots that took months to fill are being burned in days so that the Erusean army cannot use them.

At Los Canas the allied command is digging in. Engineers are laying mines across the approaches, and the harbour is crowded with ships waiting to evacuate the wounded. The staff officers do not use the word "defeat" in their reports. They write about consolidation, about regrouping, and about time — the one thing the allies still have and Erusea, overstretched across a continent, does not.

fields.text: ISAF headquarters moves to North Point
lines: ISAF headquarters moves to North Point

fields.text:
The headquarters moved by night, in convoys of ships with their lights off.

ISAF has left the continent. Its command, its records and its surviving air wings are now based on North Point, the island nation beyond the reach of Stonehenge's guns. The official chronology records that ISAF established its headquarters in North Point on 16 September 2004.

From the island, the allied command is rebuilding: training new pilots on runways the railguns cannot touch, repairing ships in North Point's yards, and planning a return that the Erusean broadcasts insist will never come. On the continent, the occupied cities wait. Some of the people in them listen to North Point's radio station at night, with the volume turned low.

fields.text: ISAF lands on the Usean continent
lines: ISAF lands on the Usean continent

fields.text:
Before dawn, the first landing craft hit the beaches.

After a year of preparation on North Point, ISAF has returned to the Usean continent. The official chronology records that ISAF landed on 24 January 2005. Allied aircraft are flying cover from forward strips cut out of farmland. Behind the first waves come engineers, fuel bladders and the long tail of an army that intends to stay.

The Erusean command, which has spent a year holding a continent with an army built for a short war, now has to decide where to defend and what to give up. Along the occupied roads, people have started taking down the posters.

fields.text: Stonehenge is destroyed
lines: Stonehenge is destroyed

fields.text:
For the first time since the war began, allied aircraft are flying over the San Salvacion desert without dying.

ISAF has destroyed Stonehenge. The official chronology records that the battery was destroyed on 2 April 2005, with seven of its eight railguns knocked out. The strike crews who came back from the desert do not say much about it.

The weapon was built to protect Usea from Ulysses, under an international project that was meant to belong to everyone. It has ended as a ruin, after two years of being turned against the people it was built for. Allied commanders note that Erusea has lost its shield in the sky. The engineers who designed the battery are less ready to celebrate.

the sky. The engineers who designed the battery are less ready to
celebrate.

lines: The Mount Shezna radar

fields.text:
The radar station on Mount Shezna is gone.

The official chronology records that the Mount Shezna radar was destroyed on 10 October 2004, to cover ISAF's retreat from Saint Ark. With the radar silenced, the allied columns pulling back from Saint Ark had a chance to get clear. Nobody on the staff pretends it was anything but a retreat; everybody agrees it was a retreat that kept an army alive.

lines: The Aegir fleet at Comberth Harbor

fields.text:
Comberth Harbor is full of burning ships.

The official chronology records that ISAF sank Erusea's Aegir fleet at Comberth Harbor on 23 November 2004. The fleet that was meant to keep the allies off the continent is gone. In the coastal towns, people watched the smoke for hours.

lines: Air battle over the Comona Islands

fields.text:
The sky over the Comona Islands was full of contrails by noon on the last day of the year.

The official chronology records a large air battle over the Comona Islands on 31 December 2004. On North Point, the staff officers planning the return to the continent read the after-action reports twice. For the first time in a long time, they were not reading about losses alone.

fields.text:
Istas Fortress has fallen, and the Tango Line is broken.

The official chronology records that ISAF took Istas Fortress and breached the Tango Line on 28 February 2005. Allied columns are moving through the gap into country that has not seen allied uniforms since the war began.

They came out through the desert at night, families and all.

lines: The northern landing at Ice Creek

lines: The Whiskey Corridor

The Whiskey Corridor has been breached.

fields.text: Erusea asks for an armistice
lines: Erusea asks for an armistice

fields.text:
The request came through a neutral embassy, written in the formal language of surrender negotiations without using the word.

Erusea proposes an armistice along the current front lines. Its envoys say that the war has cost both sides more than either can afford, and that the continent needs reconstruction more than it needs a victor. They offer to stop where the armies stand and to talk about everything else afterwards.

Our generals are divided. Some believe Erusea is near breaking and that an armistice now would let it rebuild for another war. Others point to the casualty lists and the empty treasury. Accepting ends the war without a decision. Refusing means fighting on to the end, wherever that is.

fields.text: ISAF offers an armistice
lines: ISAF offers an armistice

fields.text:
ISAF's offer was broadcast openly, so that the Erusean people would hear it at the same time as their government.

The allied command proposes an armistice along the current front lines. The fighting would stop where the armies stand; borders, prisoners and Stonehenge would be settled at a conference afterwards. The offer is generous. It is also a test of whether the government in Farbanti can still afford to say no.

Accepting ends the war without a decision on the battlefield. Refusing commits Erusea to fighting on.

fields.text: Farbanti falls
lines: Farbanti falls

fields.text:
FARBANTI — The Erusean capital has fallen, and the Usean Continental War is over.

Allied columns entered Farbanti's outskirts this week after a final offensive across the continent. The official chronology records that Farbanti fell and Erusea surrendered on 19 September 2005. Reporters describe white sheets hanging from apartment windows, Erusean soldiers stacking their rifles in the squares, and crowds that cannot decide whether to cheer or weep.

Two years after the invasion of San Salvacion, ISAF has done what its critics said it could not. The cost is still being counted: cities damaged in the fighting, a generation of pilots lost, and a continent that came through a falling sky only to tear itself apart.

Allied officers warn that the surrender has not ended every danger. Some Erusean units have not answered the order to lay down arms.

fields.text: Erusea wins the Continental War
lines: Erusea wins the Continental War

fields.text:
The broadcasts from Farbanti have been triumphant for a week.

Central Usea's command has collapsed. Its armies have capitulated or scattered, its allies are seeking terms, and Erusea's forces dominate the continent from San Salvacion to the coast. In the occupied capitals, Erusean administrators are moving into ministries whose previous occupants have fled or been arrested.

In the official chronology, ISAF wins the Continental War. In this campaign Erusea has won it, and the order that follows will be written in Farbanti.

fields.text: An armistice in Usea
lines: An armistice in Usea

fields.text:
The guns along the front have stopped, and nobody has won.

An armistice now holds between Erusea and the allied governments along the front lines as they stood on the day it was signed. Neither side has the strength to break the other, and both have agreed to stop trying, for now. Prisoners will be exchanged and commissions will meet. The maps in every staff headquarters show a line that both sides call temporary.

In the official chronology, ISAF wins the Continental War. In this campaign the war has ended in a stalemate, and the continent will have to live with a border drawn by exhaustion.

fields.text: Megalith
lines: Megalith

fields.text:
The surrender is barely a week old when the reports start coming in.

Young Erusean officers, refusing their government's order to lay down arms, have seized Megalith, a fortress built to bring down orbiting Ulysses fragments. Allied intelligence knows little about it beyond its purpose, and that purpose is enough. A weapon built to bring down fragments of Ulysses is now in the hands of men who refused to surrender.

The official chronology records that young Erusean officers seized Megalith on 26 September 2005. ISAF must take the fortress before it can be used. The pilots chosen for the mission have been told only that it may be the last flight of the war.

fields.text: Megalith is destroyed
lines: Megalith is destroyed

fields.text:
Megalith is silent.

The allied strike group went in under the fortress's defences and came out again with fewer aircraft than it took. The reports from the cockpits are fragmentary and the debriefings run long. Whatever the officers who seized it meant to do, they will not do it now.

The war is over. This time, nobody is broadcasting otherwise.

fields.text: Erusea's provisional government
lines: Erusea's provisional government

fields.text:
Erusea will govern itself again, under oversight.

The official chronology records that after Megalith was destroyed, Erusea formed a provisional autonomous government under ISAF oversight. The new administration has inherited a country with damaged cities, an army in camps and a population that lived through both a falling sky and a lost war in six years.

In this campaign the government in office remains in place. The oversight arrangement is shown as a national spirit, not a change of borders or ideology. What Erusea becomes now is a question for the years after 2005.

fields.text: Usea at the end of the war
lines: Usea at the end of the war

fields.text:
The year closes, and the archivists have started their work.

Refugee pressure stands at [?ac_ucw_pressure|.0]. Fallout recovery stands at [?ac_ucw_recovery|.0]. [GetUcwOutcome]

Six years have passed since Ulysses broke apart over the world. Usea has been shaped by the decisions taken in that time: borders opened or closed, talks accepted or refused, a war fought or averted. Some of the ministries that drafted the first fallout brief no longer exist. Many of the people who walked toward the borders in 2000 have not gone home, and some of them never will.

This is the end of the authored Usean chronology. The campaign continues; what comes next has not yet been written.

fields.text: The Telephone That Everyone Calls
lines: The Telephone That Everyone Calls

fields.text: A district operator has pinned three unofficial numbers beside the official switchboard. They reach the people who can find a water crew, open a shelter or explain why a receiving office is shut. None appears in the national register. Publishing the contact list would make a fragile local arrangement into a public service; keeping it within the rota would leave operators freer to improvise. The choice is who can demand an answer when a familiar voice is no longer there.

fields.text: The Key in the Wrong Office
lines: The Key in the Wrong Office

fields.text: An inspection has found a sound shelter whose key is held by an office that closes before the evening protection rota begins. Everyone involved followed a written instruction. The protection service can fund a joint receiving desk and rebuild institutional capacity, or put dispatchers on an immediate priority footing so the next practical allocation need not wait. Neither course creates more staff; it changes how the existing service uses them.

fields.text: A Forecast on Every Noticeboard
lines: A Forecast on Every Noticeboard

fields.text: The warning has produced notices that disagree in small but important ways. A protection officer asks for practical instruction cards explaining where uncertainty remains. Dispatch staff ask instead for time to revise the movement chain. The first choice strengthens preparation completed before the crisis boundary; the second improves a military and service capability that remains useful afterward. Neither can promise safety simply by printing a confident sentence.

fields.text: The Receiving Office Is Full
lines: The Receiving Office Is Full

fields.text: A neighbouring service asks whether San Salvacion can accept another set of urgent requests. The local receiving desk is already carrying cases that were never assigned a destination. What cannot be offered is capacity that the country has only counted twice.

An inspected restoration will rebuild local capacity and leave an honest gap in the evidence. A rapid operational restart will give dispatch work precedence and reopen the next review allocation. The service must choose what it can responsibly promise, rather than declare every missing record found.

fields.text: The Network's Ordinary Year
lines: The Network's Ordinary Year

fields.text: The national programme now has a record of what survived, what was refused and what had to be done under external conditions. Its conclusion does not decide the war or erase the settlement. The government can renew an ordinary civil service whose future funded completions support recovery, or retain a bounded readiness record at a continuing public cost. Either choice is an ongoing obligation, not a final gift from the calendar.

lines: Two Owners of the Same Timetable

fields.text: A workshop's delivery book and a public receiving office both reserve the same morning movement. Amber can publish a common record, accepting the public cost of explaining which bargain had to wait, or maintain a restricted operational schedule and concentrate on dispatch capability. The timetable is a development policy before it becomes a relief plan.

accept its continuing public burden, or keep the working list restricted and
strengthen operational coordination. The finite slot limit remains in either case.

An immediate operational allocation can instead resolve the next practical task without waiting for a further rota. The reserve authority must record which commitment was left unmet.

fields.text: The warning has made every unused corner of a depot look like a national reserve. Dispatchers want to concentrate on the receiving chain and the transport already available. Ugellas can improve one without pretending it has found unlimited storage, drivers or fuel. Work completed afterward will be response rather than earlier preparation.

fields.text:
On 31 December 1995, Robert Tyler, commander of the FCU Army Southern District, eliminates a rebel base in the Skully Islands. Unified Command defeats the rebel forces there through the actions of Scarface Squadron (ACES Chronicle, 1995 / 12.31).

fields.text: Nation In Pieces
lines: Nation In Pieces

fields.text: Our nation is in pain. The continued overspending on the military has wrecked our economy, which in turn has caused businesses to downsize, laying off workers, making them spend less, further drying up economic growth, causing company after company to close their doors. Without the goods and services offered by many of these companies, it has gotten harder and harder for our citizens to source food, pay bills, or provide for their families. This, in turn, has caused drastically increased radicalization and polarization of our populace, who turn to radical idealisms as their only hope of change. Even worse, due to our nation being in this state for quite some time, even our resources in the government are now beginning to run thin.

fields.text: People On The Streets
lines: People On The Streets

fields.text: The scope of the protests is far greater than we ever imagined. Nearly every day has some kind of major protest happening somewhere in our country, and crimes have also seen exponential growth compared to when this all began. Masses of people are calling for all sorts of demands, from more reform programs all the way to calls for outright revolution. The silver lining in this is that the sheer mass of protesters makes them unable to unite or organize effectively, making them less of a threat than an organized group. Regardless, this will only buy us some time, as if we continue to leave this issue unresolved they will no doubt find a way to organize.

fields.text: Economy Long Gone
lines: Economy Long Gone

fields.text: Our economy has had negative growth for over a year now, and the effects are extremely obvious. The vast majority of our nation lives below the poverty line, as the middle class has been all but obliterated. More than half of the small businesses in the country have closed, and about a third of the large businesses went bankrupt or were bought out. International companies and investors saw the writing on the wall long ago and have left for greener pastures, meaning there's no external group we can use to leverage ourselves back onto our feet. Worst of all, now our own funds in the government have begun to dry up, and we've had to downsize our own government and print larger amounts of currency to offset our expenses. However, even that is wearing thin and the inflation is devaluing our money faster than we can print enough to compensate it.

fields.text: Mass Exodus
lines: Mass Exodus

fields.text: Unemployment is only the tip of the iceberg. Workers, scientists, doctors, lawyers, even our own officials are emigrating to other countries to find work, and at an alarming rate. The lack of job opportunities in Belka is causing workers to look elsewhere, even outside their home country, to provide for their families. Some are even taking their families with them. Houses run empty and border checkpoints are crowded as people scramble to exit the country. Not only have we lost our workforce, but we will be unable to recover them if we cannot stop this outflow of people. If this keeps up, there won't even be a Belka to revive.

fields.text: Complete Collapse
lines: Complete Collapse

fields.text: It appears, ironically, that our last efforts to take inventory on the crisis pushed us over the tipping point. Our budget this month was unable to meet the expenses, and as a result we, as a nation, are in complete bankruptcy. As our officials find out, many are simply getting up and leaving. We are completely powerless and at the whims of whatever the future brings. The only influence we have is off goodwill alone, and that will not get us far. The future is dark.

Belka is in a state of anarchy. It is impossible to even tell what is happening in the country because all sources of information we could use is gone or takes orders from someone new now. Dinsmark is empty.

fields.text: New Elections, New Rule
lines: New Elections, New Rule

fields.text: After the collapse of the BCNP's administration, an emergency election was called by the Alternative Wege to regain control of the government. Unsurprisingly, they came out on top, with the BNCP scattered between the DLP, Wege itself, and the rest joining the monarchist movement. With the liberals now in power and promising to fix the mistakes of the past no matter how difficult it may be, a sliver of hope has returned that new leaders may bring about change.

fields.text: Osean Proposition
lines: Osean Proposition

fields.text: Our longtime rival, the Osean Federation, have approached us with an interesting offer. In return for giving several of our eastern territories to the neighboring countries, and selling a portion of the Great Lakes to Osea itself, the Oseans will pay us a rather high sum of money, giving us the ability to start some recovery programs. Osea has even expressed that they would be willing to lease many of the resources in the area to us through a joint resource excavation company. Some in the government are suspicious of this deal, since it's unlikley that Osea would offer us such a deal without a clear benefit to them, but others are hopeful that it could be the beginning of a new era of cooperation between our nations, as well as our lifeline to save our nation. It is a rather humiliating deal to take, but what other choice do we have?

lines: Selling Of The Land

fields.text: With all the paperwork in place, we've agreed to the Oseans' proposal and are preparing to remove our forces from the land. The transactions have been made and we now have enough money to get a few programs going. For their cooperation, [BLK.GetLeader] has suggested we take the Oseans up on their joint resource company offer, something that will give us a reliable income from which to rebuild the rest of our country off of.

lines: GLRDC Goes Live

fields.text: The Great Lakes Resource Development Company opened up today, marking our second cooperation with the Oseans. Early reports have showed us promising amounts of resources in the area, meaning this will likely be a very lucrative deal. Digging has begun and we've invested more of our money into the program to see a profit as quickly as we can. Things are looking up for us, we may just be able to refloat our economy with this.

fields.text: The Results Are In
lines: The Results Are In

fields.text:
They lied to us. 

 The Oseans lied to us about the resources. There weren't even any to begin with in that area. To add insult to injury, we're getting reports in the eastern countries that the territories we sold have plentiful resources in them, that now those countries are exploiting to their full potential. We are now down almost all the money we got from the original deal, and now there does not appear to be any sort of tool or program we can use to save ourselves.

fields.text: Total Anarchy
lines: Total Anarchy

fields.text: After the news of the Osean scam got out, the public has been whirled back into a frenzy, and our attempts at damage control seem to have completely failed. We've run out of money again, and now the [BLK.GetRulingParty] is seeing mass defections to the communists and monarchists. The public is completely uncontrollable and the nation is in complete anarchy.

fields.text: New Power At The Top
lines: New Power At The Top

fields.text: Over the past few days, an intense battle between the DLP and the monarchists ensued across the country, with the DLP now the undisputed dominant power in the country. With the DLP's support in the military assisting them, they have secured control over all apparatuses of state and now are the new leaders of the country, with most of the opposition imprisoned or jailed. With its third government in the last few months, it remains to be seen if the DLP will solve any of the issues plaguing the country.

fields.text: Many People, One Nation, One Goal
lines: Many People, One Nation, One Goal

fields.text: Belka has been wounded, not just by her enemies but also by her own supposed leaders, each of whom pulled her apart seeking their own goals. The failiures of the previous governments showed they were not fit to lead Belka. Now it is our turn. We will unite the people and raise Belka from the ashes, ascendent to the top of the world. With no one left to stand in our way, the DLP will restore Belka to its former glory and beyond. We have much to do, and the people's patience is thin because of the past, so we must waste no time in getting to work. Many of our members have already put forward ideas to start our recovery, which will provide us with a head start on our recovery.

fields.text: The 2 Year Plan
lines: The 2 Year Plan

fields.text: After intense discussion, we have arrived at a conclusion on how to start our reconstruction. While the military is all we have left, and is necessary for our self-preservation, this is exactly what we will use to our advantage. Converting a large amount of our military production into civilan will allow us to start economic growth without many funds to go off of, and our military is powerful enough as it is to ward off any potential invasions from Osea. This will upset the militarist faction in our government, but in all likelyhood they will come around when our economy recovers, which we can use to expand the military from once again.

fields.text: Magic Of Bureaucracy
lines: Magic Of Bureaucracy

fields.text: Through some decisive means, we've found a way to get back at those wretched Oseans. We still technically have a share in the Great Lakes Resource Development Company, but who said we have to use it for that purpose? Using some underhanded methods and pulling strings, we've managed to convert some of the resources used in that project to produce some industry for our own benefit. This will only work for so long before either the Oseans find out and shut down the company, or the company itself dries up, but it's a nice boost, and one that sticks it to the Oseans.

fields.text: Harsh Countermeasures
lines: Harsh Countermeasures

fields.text: Getting jobs for the unemployed is a rather large task, however a mitigation we can use to still get some usable labor is by introducing forced labor and community service for prisoners in our nation. To bolster these numbers, we have criminalized emigration and remaining unemployed, which should hopefully give us an edge against unemployment, at the cost of some public opinion.

fields.text: Regulate Trade Policy
lines: Regulate Trade Policy

fields.text: To recover our economy, we'll need to prompt trade with other nations, but we need to make sure we're gaining a strong profit from it. Rather than allow companies to do free business, we'll make sure that any trade goes through us before it is approved, allowing us to take a cut of the sale, letting us improve the economy itself. With any luck, this process will repeat exponentially, encouraging investors despite the tax of our government on their transactions.

companies to do free business, we'll make sure that any trade goes through us
before it is approved, allowing us to take a cut of the sale, letting us improve the
economy itself. With any luck, this process will repeat exponentially,
encouraging investors despite the tax of our government on their transactions.

fields.text: Clashes Within The Party
lines: Clashes Within The Party

fields.text: We always expected opposition, at least from the public, and from within our own party to an extent, but we didn't expect it to be around this long. We've begun a number of recovery programs and are already seeing the first fruits of recovery, and yet the militarist faction of our government led by Waldemarr Rald has only dissented louder and louder with each reform that we make, cutting into the military's budget. Unfortunately for us, many of the close-minded officers and generals in the Belkan Armed Forces are seeing these budget cuts as attacks on their livelihood and siding with Rald. It's begun to affect our ability in decision-making, meaning we'll likely need to find a way to please Rald and his militarists.

Worryingly, many of the heads of the Armed Forces have come forward announcing support for Rald, but despite this outflow of support he has yet to make any appearances.

fields.text: Total War
lines: Total War

fields.text: The humliation and shame inflicted on us not just by Osea, but also the foolish conservatives who allowed Belkan territory to secede in the 1987 Federal Law Review, cannot be allowed to stand. Waldemarr Rald held a meeting with his cabinet today promising an immenent revenge war against Osea and the former states, reclaiming lost Belkan territory, as soon as the military is restored back to its former level. While he has not gone public with this information, he has constantly blamed Osea and the other nations for poisoning Belka, and promises citizens that things will be made right. Rald promises to his cabinet a state of 'total war,' as he describes it- 'To wage war with all tools, methods, resources, and weapons that you have at your disposal, to fight tooth and nail with everything you have until victory or annhilation.'

fields.text: Excalibur Online
lines: Excalibur Online

fields.text: Excalibur, the chemical laser anti-ICBM system devised as a part of the large military build-up of the past couple decades, has finally been finished with our efforts. The designs have changed slightly since the original proposed design from 1981, however the core design has remained mostly unchanged. These designs have allowed us to make the design more modular, including swappable lenses for different ranges and targets, as well as heat transferring pipes to allow the main structure to assist in cooling as well as the six primary cooling towers. This also has allowed for possible future improvements on the design, but for now we have a simple choice to make on where to invest the last of the project's leftover budget. We could develop an electronic targeting system that syncs up with radar data, allowing Excalibur to easily target agile objects like aircraft, boosting our air superiority capabilities. We could even invest in a denser power system, allowing the laser to reach higher temperatures and give it the ability to assist in ground attacks. Or we could simply keep it to its original purpose and improve its ICBM destruction capabilities.

fields.text: Religion is a large part of people's lives in Belka, and for the church to disagree with the state would cause dissent within the nation. To combat this, Waldemarr Rald has decided to declare the United Church of Belka, to ensure that the church does not teach dissenting thoughts against the state. This new organization will need a leader from the religious sector that will not be seen as a mere puppet. The three best possible candidates have been presented to Rald, and we now await his answer. Father Hannes Kellermann, head of the Church of Dinsmark, has been an outspoken loyalist of the DLP and while he was originally supportive of the pacifist wing of the party, has since come around and speaks extremely positively of Rald. He may not be very useful aside from his high charisma and undying loyalty, but the church will never be an issue as long as he is around. Opposite of him is Father Arnold Weinmann, a leading figure in the Lumen Cathedral, originally a member of the Alternative Wege, but reluctantly changed to the DLP after accusations of Osean sympathies. He is not an Osean sympathizer, however he greatly prefers the pacifist wing of the DLP, and has yet to endorse Rald publicly, making his loyalty questionable. Despite that, he used to work as an economist during the military build-up several years ago, and likely could be of use in that area, assisting with our own build-up. Finally, we have Father Wilfried Jan Riese von Sergio Luoni, a former bishop from Hoffnung, who was removed from position after declaring many sects as heretical and claiming only he had the true interpretation of the Scriptures. He has since been excommunicated, but leads a small cult-like following in Sudentor, mostly popular with lower-class people and occultists. He is a wild card, loyalty unknown and likely would not serve any extra benefits, however his leadership would keep the Church far from government affairs, as it would be too busy fighting itself to make any targeted effort agains the government.

fields.text: Expanding our military will require expanding command just as much as recruiting more soldiers, and for that we must make a choice of where our new leaders will come from. Some younger members of the DLP are involved with the Belkan Army, and while they may not be the cream of the crop, their ideological loyalty may be worth it if a campaign does not go well, where a lesser general may retreat or surrender. Alternatively, the Belkan Officer Academy always allows the best to rise to the top, however the students there belong to a wide variety of ideologies, and as such their quality might be offset by their loyalty to our cause.

fields.text: The idea of Belka must be firmly rooted in the mind of each soldier, worker, and citizen of Belka. Not the Belka of today, not the government of Belka nor its people or its land. Belkans must be obsessed with the idea of a Belka that is greater than anything we could imagine now. Closer than family, than work, than religion, than life itself. So close that they are willing to fight, work and die to achieve it. Raising Belka to the status of a deity that we owe our lives, that we must serve with all we have. A Belka that is timeless and infinite, a Belka that is strong to its core. A Belka over all.

fields.text: Resources in Ustio
lines: Resources in Ustio

fields.text: Yesterday, a news report was published in Ustio detailing mass deposits of precious metals beneath the surface of its mountains, extremely close to the surface, with the land market exploding overnight. Rald is beside himself with fury at the news, claiming that Ustio should cede all resource rights to Belka, as the resources had not been discovered when the conservatives foolishly allowed the Ustians to secede. With the new money, Ustio has already announced several new programs to stabilize themselves, much to our dismay. A small paper trail suggests that Osea might also have been intentionally hiding these resources until Ustio declared its independence, also lending credibility to the theory that Osea funded Ustian independence movements as well. Rald has declared to his cabinet that this has been the last straw, and is preparing the military for imminent war within the next six months.

fields.text: Attack on Excalibur
lines: Attack on Excalibur

fields.text: Excalibur, our chemical laser anti-ICBM weapon, has been destroyed in a massive raid by the Osean Air Defense Force and Ustian Air Force, completely eliminating its viability. Despite massive losses and fierce resistance from our forces, the four RTLS systems and the surrounding support weapons were slowly picked off by the aircraft, before destroying the lens itself, then finally targeting the central structure until it collapsed, rendering it completely unsalvageable. While we still own the territory underneath Excalibur, the weapon is completely unusable and would not be repairable without a complete rebuilding of the structure. While this does not mean a complete loss, this will greatly set back our ability to project power around our nation, and we will need to be much more careful about which battles we have the capacity to fight in the future.

fields.text: The Belkan War
lines: The Belkan War

fields.text:
The Belkan War was a large scale conflict that took part between the 25th of March, 1995 and June 20th of the same year. It involved two of the largest superpowers of the world, being the bellicose nation of Belka and the Osean Federation with addition of all other Belkan neighbors. It all started after an unprecedented economic crisis hit Belka a decade earlier, leading to territorial concessions and a desperate population to seek hope and revenge in a far-right, militarist party, who used all Belka's remaining economic might to wage war against Ustio, a country that recently seceded and found enormous amounts of resources.

Thus, Belka declared war on all surrounding countries in a last-ditch attempt to gain supremacy in the Osean continent and regain all lost territories. After an initial setback, the attacked countries formed an alliance that counterattacked and pushed back Belkan forces, expoliting the inability of Belkan state to sustain equipment losses. With rumors, later confirmed, of Belka developing weapons of mass destruction, Allied forces continued to penetrate Belkan lands leading to the secession of the southern part of the nation, until the Belkan government, in a desperate attempt to save the northern part of the country, launched a nuclear attack along the Waldreich Mountains on June 6th, 1995.

Seeing the insanity unfold, the Allies accepted Belka's sue for peace resulting in the peace conference of Lumen of June 20th.
